findings.disposition: Cloud target profile currently contains static instance/VPC declarations, certificate pin and artifact/case checks, but it has no signed TargetGrant or control-plane attestation that the writable target is the declared RDS instance/VPC. The local ledger now persists planned resource names before execution and fails closed on unproven ownership, but no real PostgreSQL proof has exercised transaction rollback, 20-way CAS, or crash boundaries from requested through each DDL and cleanup step.

A crash after CREATE and before OID ownership persistence must remain failed_cleanup with explicit operator evidence; the runner must never infer ownership or delete by name alone. This path lacks a real cloud recovery receipt.

A slot created only at dispatch would permit a new idempotency key after an earlier pre-dispatch terminal. The implementation requires a server-derived canonical header per business revision before it can claim a complete logical-node cap.
Tests must distinguish one valid dispatch exactly once from each rejected path at zero; a generic zero-or-one assertion is insufficient.
The initial binding inventory must explicitly cover planning, question generation, evaluation including quote repair, quiz, diagnosis, and report before it can claim every current text node.
